channel.description: Latest articles from Scripps Institution of Oceanography – Bias and Credibility (scripps.ucsd.edu)

item.title: Ask a Scientist: How Do the Polar Regions Impact You?
item.description: For the past three decades, glaciologist Helen Amanda Fricker has been investigating polar regions — the fastest changing areas on Earth. By studying the Arctic and Antarctic, she and other scientists are uncovering how the planet is responding to climate change, from melting ice and rising seas to shifting ocean currents and extreme weather patterns.

item.title: Fund for Science and Technology Awards $15 Million to Scripps Oceanography
item.description: Scripps Institution of Oceanography at the University of California San Diego has received a $15 million grant from the Fund for Science and Technology (FFST). This support will expand observational capabilities into parts of the ocean where data has historically been sparse or nonexistent. The resulting insights will help scientists understand how the ocean is changing and what those changes mean for the planet.

item.title: Scripps Student Spotlight: Kris Wang
item.description: Kris Wang is a fourth-year undergraduate student at Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego, where he is studying geosciences with a focus on volcanology and igneous petrology.

item.title: Researchers Create a Family History of San Diego Kelp over More Than Four Decades
item.description: Key takeaways– Giant kelp forests, an icon of the San Diego coastline, are in retreat as a result of climate change– Off the coast, water temperature has not dropped to traditional lows since the 2015 appearance of a warm mass of water in the eastern Pacific Ocean– A new study illustrates the importance of long-term observations to guide conservation efforts

item.title: UC San Diego Experts Bring Innovative Discoveries to the Global Stage at SXSW 2026
item.description: Leading experts from the University of California San Diego are set to return to Austin, Texas, for the annual South by Southwest (SXSW) conference to showcase groundbreaking research and innovation to a global audience. From March 12-18, they will join a diverse community of researchers, industry leaders and changemakers from around the world at SXSW for opportunities to network, learn and discover.

item.title: Dance Party Turns Up the Volume on Climate Action
item.description: At a time when climate conversations can feel overwhelming, a new celebration is flipping the script with music, movement and momentum! Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego and Birch Aquarium are teaming up to throw a Climate Dance Party that brings together ocean science, climate solutions and a whole lot of joy.

item.title: California Communities’ Recovery Time Between Wildfire Smoke Events Is Shrinking
item.description: Californians have long dealt with wildfire smoke as a seasonal fact of life, but those fires have become more intense and frequent, raising the profile of wildfire smoke as a public health issue. Now, a study led by researchers at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography finds that the time between multi-day smoke events is shrinking — leaving communities with less time to recover before smoke returns.

item.title: Human-Made Chemicals Found Throughout Ocean Environments
item.description: A new study analyzing more than 2,300 seawater samples from around the world has found that human-made chemicals — from plastic additives and industrial lubricants to pharmaceuticals and pesticides — are widespread in the marine environment, particularly in coastal and estuarine waters.

item.title: Nicole Yen’s Passion for Marine Science Inspires the Next Generation of Leaders
item.description: When Nicole Yen isn’t in the ocean herself, she’s studying its mysteries and inspiring the next generation of scientists to dive in and explore it, too. She discovered her love for the ocean and its inhabitants while earning her undergraduate degree at UC San Diego in biology with a focus on ecology, behavior and evolution, and a minor in marine science.

item.title: Two Scripps-Named Marine Species Make Top 10 List
item.description: Glittery sea worms and sea squirts fit for The Lord of the Rings universe might sound like pure fantasy, but they’re very real creatures living in the deep sea. Some of these otherworldly ocean animals are even featured in the latest “Top 10 New Marine Species” list published by the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS).
